suite.description: Draft held-out product-fit final evaluation manifest. Documents are fixed; questions must be generated and frozen before any system run.

ragas_context_policy.native: Score each system against the context it generated from. Helpmate uses full selected evidence; vendor answers use the capped context passed into their generator.
ragas_context_policy.equalized: Score all systems against the same top-k and max-character context cap.

results.question: How do the cumulative and per-year investment requirements differ between the Planned Energy Scenario and the 1.5 degree C Scenario?
results.answer_preview: The Planned Energy Scenario requires USD 103 trillion in cumulative energy sector investments for 2023-2050, while the 1.5°C Scenario requires USD 150 trillion, which is USD 47 trillion more. For annual investment, the evidence says the 1.5°C pathway needs an additional USD 1.7 trillion per year compared with the Planned Energy Scenario, and around USD 1 trillion per year of fossil fuel-based investments envisaged in the Planned Energy Scenario must be redirected to energy transition technologie
results.note: The evidence provides both cumulative totals and the difference between scenarios. Source 3 states the Planned Energy Scenario cumulative investment is USD 103 trillion and the 1.5°C Scenario is USD 150 trillion, with USD +47 trillion more. It also states the difference in annual investment is USD +1.7 trillion per year. Source 1 adds that around USD 1 trillion of annual fossil fuel-based investments in the Planned Energy Scenario must be redirected, but the direct annual comparison between scenarios is the USD 1.7 trillion figure in Source 3.
